title: pre-commit hook blocks commits on pre-existing PHPCS warnings
body:
## Problem

`.githooks/pre-commit` runs `vendor/bin/phpcs --colors "$FILE"` and treats any non-zero exit as failure. PHPCS exits 1 when a file has **warnings only**. Any edit to a file with pre-existing warnings is therefore blocked, even when the change adds no errors.

Example: `inc/models/class-base-model.php` has 6 pre-existing warnings (`PSR2.Classes.PropertyDeclaration.Underscore` on `$_original`, `$_mappings`, `$_mocked`; `Squiz.PHP.CommentedOutCode.Found` at about lines 732/737; `PSR2.Methods.MethodDeclaration.Underscore` on `_get_original`) and 0 errors. Committing #2004 failed with "Could not fully fix", and PHPCBF reported "No fixable errors were found".

## Fix

- File: `.githooks/pre-commit` (the `phpcs` calls at about lines 42, 60 and 75).
- Make the pass/fail checks ignore warnings, e.g. `vendor/bin/phpcs -n` or `--runtime-set ignore_warnings_on_exit 1`. Still show warnings for information if needed.

## Verification

- Stage a whitespace-only change to `inc/models/class-base-model.php` and run `git commit`. The hook passes, and PHPStan still runs.
- Stage a real PHPCS error (e.g. a non-Yoda comparison in `inc/`). The hook still blocks the commit.

### Files Scope

- `.githooks/pre-commit`
